answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique ski instructor certification. With a certificate plus seasons taught at one resort, a single quill check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the canyon of that gap is the whole defence in one line. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the relic of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
